title: Inflation higher than expected. CNN rolls tape on Trump's economic promises
summary: CNN reviews the hot September 2026 CPI against the president's promises: strong jobs and GDP, but inflation above where it started, war-driven fuel costs and shrinking real wages.

assertions.quote: But prices will come down. You just watch, you'll come down and they'll come down fast.

verdicts.note: The CPI has risen about three to four percent a year through 2026; broad price declines occur only in deep recessions.

assertions.quote: The economy is the greatest economy we've ever had by far.
That war is going to end very soon. And when it does, your prices are going to come tumbling down. They already are.
The economy looks great. Actually, unemployment is at 4.2%. We call that full employment. Retail sales 1.2%. People keep spending despite high prices.

verdicts.note: In 2026 real hourly earnings fell 0.7% over the year while real GDP grew 2.5% and 2.2% annualized in Q1 and Q2 and unemployment held at 4.1-4.3%, showing growth and falling purchasing power coexisting; but job gains were weak (+29,000 in September, 45,000/month average), so the employment side was steady rather than strong.

assertions.quote: The fingerprints of the war are all over this report.
for six months in a row, for the half a year, real wages adjusted for inflation, they're getting smaller
inflation is higher right now than it was when the president started his second term
That's above the overall rate of inflation. And that reflects in part a lot of demand driven by the AI boom.

verdicts.note: Data-center load is raising wholesale power demand and memory chip shortages lifted computer prices, but fuel costs and grid investment also drive electricity bills.

assertions.quote: food at home. This is groceries up by less than 2%. This is the best number of the of the president's second term.

verdicts.note: Food-at-home inflation ran below overall inflation in late 2026 according to the CPI release, though rising diesel costs threaten that.

Food at home rose 1.8% over the 12 months to September 2026 with monthly changes of -0.1%, 0.0% and -0.1% in July-September, and the broader food index slowed from 3.2% (April 2026) to 2.5%; beef fell 1.0% and dairy 0.9% on the month.

assertions.quote: diesel is near all time highs. That's lifting the cost of transport, fuel, food.
